\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پھنسنا} (phansnā)}{پھنسنا (phansnā)}]{\ur{پھنسنا} (phansnā) — to be trapped; to be stuck}

\label{lesson:UR-C295-phansna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to rot, then the Urdu for cholera.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پھنسنا}}
\textbf{\ur{پھنسنا}} — \emph{phansnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to be trapped; to be stuck\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{تین} \ur{آدمی} \ur{ایک} \ur{کمرے} \ur{میں} \ur{پھنس} \ur{گئے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tīn ādmī ek kamre meṅ phans gae.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Three men were trapped in a room.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \ur{وہ} \ur{پھنس} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh phans gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousins \emph{phā̃snā}, \textquotedblleft{}to ensnare\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{phãsānā} under Sanskrit \emph{spāśáyati} (CDIAL 13814); \textbf{\ur{پھنسنا}} is to be caught in the snare oneself.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phansnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phansnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tīn ādmī ek kamre meṅ phans gae.} — Three men were trapped in a room.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to rot, then the Urdu for cholera, then say \emph{phansnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{پھنسنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To be trapped; to be stuck\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پکارنا} (pukārnā)}{پکارنا (pukārnā)}]{\ur{پکارنا} (pukārnā) — to call out (to)}

\label{lesson:UR-C295-pukarna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for cholera, then the Urdu for to be trapped.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پکارنا}}
\textbf{\ur{پکارنا}} — \emph{pukārnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to call out (to)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{مدد} \ur{کے} \ur{لیے} \ur{پکارا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{us ne madad ke liye pukārā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He called out for help.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{ماں} \ur{کو} \ur{پکارا}, \emph{us ne māṅ ko pukārā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پکارنا}} (\emph{pukārnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{pukārnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to shout\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*pukkār}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 8246). The person called takes \textbf{\ur{کو}}: \textbf{\ur{ماں} \ur{کو} \ur{پکارا}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pukārnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pukārnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{us ne madad ke liye pukārā.} — He called out for help.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for cholera, then the Urdu for to be trapped, then say \emph{pukārnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سناٹا} (sannāṭā)}{سناٹا (sannāṭā)}]{\ur{سناٹا} (sannāṭā) — a dead silence}

\label{lesson:UR-C295-sannata}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to be trapped, then the Urdu for to call out (to).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سناٹا}}
\textbf{\ur{سناٹا}} — \emph{sannāṭā} — \textquotedblleft{}a dead silence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{رات} \ur{کو} \ur{گلی} \ur{میں} \ur{سناٹا} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rāt ko galī meṅ sannāṭā thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At night the lane was dead silent.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سناٹا}} (\emph{sannāṭā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{sannāṭā}, \textquotedblleft{}a desolate silence\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{saṃnaṣṭa}, \textquotedblleft{}vanished\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 12925): the silence when every sound has gone.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling what happened.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{نکالنا} (nikālnā)}{نکالنا (nikālnā)}]{\ur{نکالنا} (nikālnā) — to take out; to pull out}

\label{lesson:UR-C295-nikaalna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to call out (to), then the Urdu for a dead silence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{نکالنا}}
\textbf{\ur{نکالنا}} — \emph{nikālnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to take out; to pull out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{لوگوں} \ur{نے} \ur{انہیں} \ur{باہر} \ur{نکالا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{logoṅ ne unheṅ bāhar nikālā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
People pulled them out.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{بچے} \ur{کو} \ur{نکالا}, \emph{us ne bachche ko nikālā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{nikālnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to drive out, to take out\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{niṣkālayati} (CDIAL 7484). It is the partner of \textbf{\ur{نکلنا}}: a thing \textbf{\ur{نکلنا}} by itself, and you \textbf{\ur{نکالنا}} it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nikālnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{logoṅ ne unheṅ bāhar nikālā.} — People pulled them out.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to call out (to), then the Urdu for a dead silence, then say \emph{nikālnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بے} \ur{حال} (be hāl)}{بے حال (be hāl)}]{\ur{بے} \ur{حال} (be hāl) — in a sorry state}

\label{lesson:UR-C295-be-hal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a dead silence, then the Urdu for to pull out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بے} \ur{حال}}
\textbf{\ur{بے} \ur{حال}} — \emph{be hāl} — \textquotedblleft{}in a sorry state\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وہ} \ur{بھوک} \ur{سے} \ur{بے} \ur{حال} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{voh bhūk se be hāl thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He was in a bad way from hunger.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بے} \ur{حال}} (\emph{be hāl}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{bē}, \textquotedblleft{}without\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{ḥāl}, \textquotedblleft{}a state\textquotedblright{}, a word Persian took from Arabic: without a proper state, worn out.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{be hāl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{voh bhūk se be hāl thā.} — He was in a bad way from hunger.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a dead silence, then the Urdu for to pull out, then say \emph{be hāl} again
\end{itemize}
